evals.query: Our designer wants every row in the task list of our project app to bounce in with a stagger when the list loads, and a confetti burst every time a task is completed. I'm building it in SwiftUI. Is this a good idea, and how should I build it?
expected_behavior: Gives a clear position early, with the reason.

Argues against celebration motion on an action people repeat many times a day, and proposes a quieter confirmation (for example a quick check animation or a light haptic), possibly keeping a bigger moment for a rare milestone.
Drops or limits the staggered entrance because it delays content people want to scan, or restricts it to a first appearance.
Gives concrete timing values (durations or spring parameters) for the motion it keeps.
Respects Reduce Motion with a defined alternative.
Includes SwiftUI code for the recommended approach.

evals.query: Here's how search results load in our team wiki web app today (attached). Most responses take about 80 ms, slow ones up to 2 s. Design the loading behaviour so search feels calm and fast, and give me the code.
expected_behavior: Keeps the previous results visible (or a stable placeholder) until new ones arrive, instead of clearing the list on every keystroke.
Delays any loading indicator so fast responses show none, and keeps it visible long enough not to flash once it appears.
Shortens the entrance (for example 200 ms or less, ease-out rather than ease-in) and removes or caps the 120 ms per-item stagger.
Animates only opacity and transform, not max-height or margin, so results don't shift the layout.
Debounces input or ignores out-of-order responses so stale results never replace newer ones.
